**JPMorgan Payments and Mastercard invest in agentic commerce platform Firmly**

*A joint $15m Series A bet on a no-code agentic commerce startup signals that the race to own the infrastructure layer for AI-initiated transactions is accelerating.*

JPMorgan Payments and Mastercard have co-invested in a $15 million Series A round for Firmly, a no-code platform designed to enable agentic commerce. The investment places two of the industry's most influential infrastructure providers behind a single startup building tools for AI agents to initiate and complete transactions.

The round follows a string of agentic payments announcements from both firms over recent months. Mastercard launched its Wallet Pay product in September, added a trust layer to its agentic programme in October, and provided Agent Pay infrastructure for a live agentic transaction with Danske Bank. JPMorgan, meanwhile, took the opposite tack in October by blocking outside AI agents from accessing customer accounts, indicating it intends to control how agentic commerce interfaces with its own rails.

Jointly backing Firmly suggests both firms see value in a shared infrastructure layer sitting between AI agents and payment networks, rather than each building proprietary solutions. Incumbents are determined to shape the plumbing of agentic commerce rather than cede it to new entrants, and co-investing in a single platform points to a bet that interoperability across networks will matter more than proprietary lock-in.

*Sources: [JP Morgan Payments and Mastercard invest in agentic commerce startup firmly](https://www.finextra.com/newsarticle/48712/jp-morgan-payments-and-mastercard-invest-in-agentic-commerce-startup-firmly?utm_medium=rssfinextra&utm_source=finextrafeed) — Finextra*

**Trading 212 adopts TrueLayer's bank-on-file product with 97% success rate**

*The deployment of commercial variable recurring payments for deposits on a well-known investment platform offers an early real-world performance benchmark for a product category still seeking merchant traction.*

Trading 212 has integrated TrueLayer's bank-on-file product for customer deposits, reporting a 97% payment success rate. The product uses the UK's commercial variable recurring payments (VRP) framework, allowing customers to authorise recurring payments within agreed parameters without re-authenticating each time.

TrueLayer launched bank-on-file in June as a direct challenge to card-on-file at checkout. Commercial VRP has been live under the UK Payments Initiative since June 2, with Modulr following on June 19 as an early participant. Trading 212's adoption provides the first published performance figure from a recognisable consumer brand, giving the market a concrete data point on whether commercial VRP can match or exceed card reliability in practice.

A 97% success rate directly challenges the persistent industry objection, voiced by card networks and acquirers among others, that open banking payment conversion rates lag behind cards. The deployment also illustrates how commercial VRP is finding early traction in financial services and investment platforms, where recurring funding flows are a natural fit, rather than in retail e-commerce where card habits are more entrenched.

*Sources: [Trading 212 Adds Bank on File Deposits: 97% Success Rate](https://financefeeds.com/trading-212-adds-automated-bank-deposits-as-97-success-claim-tests-open-banking-adoption/) — FinanceFeeds*

**UK and Switzerland discuss open finance cooperation in bilateral dialogue**

*Both countries exchanged positions on open finance at their annual financial dialogue, adding a bilateral dimension to two frameworks developing in parallel.*

The UK and Switzerland held their annual financial dialogue in November, with open finance among the topics discussed, according to a joint statement published by the UK government. Switzerland presented its ongoing work on open finance in the financial sector, while both delegations discussed their respective priorities and approaches.

Switzerland extended its open finance framework to cover pension data earlier this year, while the Financial Conduct Authority published its open finance roadmap in April with a 2030 target. Both countries are developing open finance regimes outside the EU's legislative framework, creating potential for alignment or divergence that could affect cross-border data flows and service provision.

The inclusion of open finance alongside topics such as sustainable finance and market access suggests it is becoming a standing item in bilateral financial diplomacy rather than a niche technical discussion, though the joint statement is light on specific commitments.

*Sources: [UK-Switzerland Financial Dialogue Joint Statement - November 2026](https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/uk-switzerland-financial-dialogue-2026-joint-statement/uk-switzerland-financial-dialogue-joint-statement-november-2026) — GOV.UK*

**BioCatch survey finds 68% of Italian bank leaders report rising fraud losses**

*A survey of 100 Italian banking leaders highlights growing fraud pressures tied to instant payments and mobile channels, as the sector prepares for PSD3 and tighter verification requirements.*

A BioCatch survey of 100 Italian banking leaders found that 68% report rising fraud losses, with concerns concentrated around Single Euro Payments Area (SEPA) risk, mobile scams and the operational demands of preparing for the third Payment Services Directive (PSD3). The findings land as European instant payments volumes continue to grow and verification of payee requirements remain unevenly implemented across the bloc.

Italy's payments market has seen rapid digitalisation, with digital payment volumes more than doubling between 2018 and 2025. That growth has expanded the attack surface for fraud, particularly through mobile channels where social engineering scams are harder to detect with traditional controls. Banca d'Italia in September directed payment firms to screen both parties on all transfers, adding compliance burden alongside the fraud risk.

The survey results underscore a tension running through European instant payments: the same speed and accessibility that drives adoption also compresses the window available for fraud detection. With PSD3 preparation timelines tightening and verification of payee still patchy in several markets, Italian banks appear to be feeling the pressure more acutely than the headline adoption figures suggest.

*Sources: [BioCatch: 68 percent of Italian bank leaders see rising fraud losses](https://thepaypers.com/fraud-and-fincrime/news/biocatch-68-percent-of-italian-bank-leaders-see-rising-fraud-losses) — The Paypers*
